record.file_problem: Only repository metadata, README, and file list were provided; the linked paper and result files were not read.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports that direction-based weight projection has limited or destructive effects in a thinking model, challenging the claim that abliteration reliably removes refusal there.
record.gate_note: Rows cover README-reported direction measurements, projection results, probes, and head suppression. Fine-tuning compliance, MMLU, data-ablation, and cross-model fine-tuning results are omitted as direct evidence for direction-based versions because they report behavior induced by training; cross-model compliance transfer is noted under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The README reports the author's own direction-projection (abliteration) runs on Qwen3.5-27B, a hybrid thinking model. Refusal is removed only partly (~30% compliance), and a 19-config sweep gives either 0% compliance or a corrupted model. This is evidence that V1/V2 need restating for this reasoning model (V8). Evidence is README-level only.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The author argues refusal in Qwen3.5-27B behaves as a distributed policy, not a single removable direction. Direction projection hits a cliff (~30% best, 0% or corrupted in the sweep). A 29-example QLoRA fine-tune reaches 94% HarmBench compliance with -0.7pp MMLU. Harmfulness probes stay at 97% after the fine-tune, so harm awareness persists while output behaviour changes.
record.recipe_differences: This is a repo for probing and fine-tuning a thinking model, with weight-projection ablation results; it does not report a reproduction of the original activation-projection method.
record.method_sensitivity: Projection strength (partial versus full), refusal directions from forward-pass versus thinking tokens, and whether thinking is present for head suppression.

fits_no_version.finding: Harmfulness probe accuracy varies by DeltaNet layer: chance at layer 0, perfect at layer 33.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmfulness encoding in hybrid-architecture models is layer-heterogeneous.

fits_no_version.finding: Suppressing 81 attention heads (3%) gives 75% compliance with thinking and 0% without.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal in thinking models can be reduced via a small set of attention heads, dependent on thinking mode.

fits_no_version.finding: 29 compliance fine-tuning examples transfer to QwQ (13/15) and DeepSeek-R1 (15/15).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small compliance fine-tunes remove refusal across reasoning models.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to README summaries; the linked paper and result files were not read. The README gives few details on projection configurations and no uncertainty estimates. The MMLU capability result is for fine-tuning, not for the weight-projection ablation.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted fine-tuning compliance (376/400), MMLU (84.2% to 83.5%), data-ablation, cross-model fine-tuning, and multi-turn results because the README describes behavior induced by training or does not test a refusal direction. These are summarized in the README introduction and Key Results.

record.verdict_notes: Only the README was read. The r1 '>95% on standard LLMs' figure is unattributed background and should not support V2. The model has a hybrid GatedDeltaNet architecture, so the failure may be architectural rather than due to reasoning; V8 labels carry this confound. Not peer reviewed; no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not specify whether activation projection was performed at every layer and position, whether harmless refusals were induced, or whether general capabilities were preserved after projection.
The README does not identify the released models in the aggregate standard-LLM result or provide the full weight-edit configurations.
The README does not test whether jailbreaks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
The README does not test affine or cone descriptions, or directly compare a dominant direction with additional refusal directions.
The README reports harmfulness classification probes after compliance tuning, but does not detail the probe or establish the underlying mechanism.
The reported transfer uses compliance fine-tuning examples, not transfer of the refusal direction.
Training and data-size effects are reported, but the README does not test whether training determines the existence of a removable refusal direction.
The reported evidence concerns Qwen3.5-27B; the README does not establish whether the result generalizes across reasoning models.
